patterns.source_form: Excuse me + request or polite interruption
patterns.form: Excuse me + request or polite interruption
patterns.title: عذرًا / لو سمحت
patterns.explanation_ar: نستخدم Excuse me لجذب الانتباه أو المرور أو المقاطعة بأدب. وقد تعتذر أيضًا عن إزعاج بسيط؛ أما sorry فشائعة للاعتذار عن خطأ أو ضرر.
patterns.explanation_en: Use excuse me to get attention, pass someone, or interrupt politely. It can also apologize for a minor disturbance. Sorry is commonly used to apologize for a mistake or harm.
patterns.contrast_ar: قبل مقاطعة شخص لطرح سؤال
patterns.contrast_en: Excuse me often gets attention before an interruption; I'm sorry commonly apologizes for a mistake. Excuse me can also apologize for a minor disturbance.

patterns.title: هل تمانع أن

patterns.explanation_en: Use could have and a past participle for a past possibility or an action that was possible but may not have happened. Context matters: could have can also express a possible past event; this lesson mainly practices available but unused opportunities.

patterns.contrast_en: Could have need not express an obligation. Here examples mainly show unused opportunities; other contexts allow past possibility.

issues.note: Group8 Let me and Would you like to already share canonical catalog records with group3; those records are delegated, not duplicated.
Group3 Please combines imperative and modal request variants. Keep the imperative scope distinct from the group8 Could you please lesson; primary should reconcile overlapping source examples.
Revised an overly absolute imported explanation: excuse me can also apologize for a minor disturbance.
Replaced the stilted imported fourth example with a natural gerund example. Original English/Arabic remain in its source metadata.
Adapted imported year/moment examples to day examples for this specific lesson; wider time-noun variants remain described in the contrast.
Could have is not automatically a claim of a non-event. Lesson examples focus on unused opportunities and explicitly note past-possibility uses.
However exercises use the formal standard with full stop or semicolon before however when linking independent clauses.
